newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures slipped amid concerns U.S. interest rates will be raised at a key monetary policy meeting later on Tuesday while interest rate futures took a cautious stance ahead of the first round in a French parliamentary election on May 25.

Analysts said the market appeared to be split on whether the Federal Reserve would raise rates for the second time this year and that it was also unclear what the likely reaction of the French bond market would be in the event of a hike.
They said French bonds would follow U.S. long bonds, but any shifts would probably be fairly muted ahead of the election.

A rise in U.S. rates would push up European bond yields if it were taken to be the precursor to further increases but could have a limited impact if seen as a timely pre-emptive move to nip U.S. inflation in the bud, analysts said.

"It's difficult. I still think if they push up rates it will be negative but it's not certain," Philippe Brossard, head of research at ABN Amro Finance, said. "It may be seen as a good move for the (U.S.) long end and in turn good for Europe."
A bond salesman at a French bank said, "If there's nothing the (French) market is more likely to go up...if there is a rise the losses will be limited."

Some futures traders said the June bond contract would be unlikely to fall much further than 129.32, a level of support tested several times at the beginning of May, from 129.64 at the close on Tuesday.

In the event of a rally in the French bond markets the first obstacle would be a gap left on charts on Tuesday between 129.82 and 129.88 with further resistance at 130.20, a prop which gave way during last Friday's slide.
Andrew Davies, analyst at London Bond Broking was doubtful U.S. bonds would provide much a spark for Europe if U.S. rates were left unchanged.
"Up to a degree U.S. bonds are taking a rather more cautious stance so if there's no change we will get a bit of a rally but don't think it will go very far," Davies said.

PIBOR contracts were lower across the board in what was described as a relatively calm session. Some said French interest rate futures may have suffered slightly from the wave of opinion polls released on Saturday before a news blackout on poll results.
The polls suggested the centre-right would win a majority in the National Assembly but showed the opposition left gaining ground in terms of voters' intentions.

"In a sense the polls...were not as good as those we saw last week. The majority of seats has narrowed and it's very close call on votes," Brossard said. "The market has been left feeling the odds are high for a conservative victory but they have not improved."
The French franc was relatively stable on Tuesday although it dipped briefly past 3.3705 against the mark before returning to 3.3672 late in the session.
Analysts said comments by French Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin that he was not committed to the stability pact on deficit control after the euro launch had little impact.
However they said such comments would clearly be taken in a more negative light if the centre-right coalition failed to retain power.
